patch.value:
## Matrix dimensions

- Requirement: every MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, supported SHOULD, removed behavior, deprecation, and error code from the official schema and changelog.
- Surface: public SDK, stdio process, Streamable HTTP process, MCP tools, resources, prompts, tasks, skills, Apps, docs, contracts, and schemas.
- Era: 2026-07-28 canonical plus every explicitly supported legacy probe and refusal.
- Outcome: positive case, malformed case, missing-capability case, unsupported-version case, concurrency case, disconnect or retry case, authorization case, resource-bound case, and negative control.
- Artifact: checkout, packed tarball, clean install, npm package, npx, bunx, and release metadata.
- Scale: deterministic ordering, prompt-cache stability, bounded output, large schema, many tools or resources, long history, and concurrent clients.
- Evidence: exact source revision, exact package version, exact commit, exact test command, gate verdict, and immutable pm record.
MCP 2026-07-28 conformance and release gate: official schema matrix, protocol-era adapters, real transports, adversarial cases, and published consumers
Build a requirement-complete test and release gate that proves the SDK, stdio server, Streamable HTTP server, packages, docs, and published artifacts implement the declared 2026-07-28 surface.

A generated matrix maps every official 2026-07-28 normative requirement and supported extension to owners and executable evidence with no unclassified row; Official schema fixtures and protocol-era tests run through the public SDK and real stdio and Streamable HTTP processes; Each major behavior has a negative control that demonstrates the gate fails when the behavior is removed or malformed; Concurrency, cancellation, disconnect, retry, replay, authorization, caching, resource bounds, and token ceilings have adversarial coverage; Packed, npm, npx, and bunx consumers execute the full canonical agent journey and verify the advertised protocol version; Release is refused if source, generated schemas, docs, contracts, server discovery, package metadata, or published behavior disagree
Turn every normative requirement and supported extension into executable local, hosted, packed, and published proof
Protocol drift, false-green tests, legacy regressions, security mistakes, and broken package bins fail before release
The existing handshake test proves an obsolete revision and the release probe validates only initialize rather than the latest protocol and extensions
